problem: Open-set, VLM-based 3D scene graphs (3DSGs) are mostly evaluated indoors, and outdoor works test on one or two scenes with narrow metrics, treating the semantic embedding space as a black box and never checking multi-session stability.
motivation: Outdoor scenes are larger, unstructured and have ambiguous terrain/object/region boundaries, so it is unclear when and why VLM-based 3DSGs fail in the field. The authors collect five outdoor datasets and use Terra as a case study to dissect embeddings, navigation, regions, memory and consistency.
key_idea: A field-report style, layer-by-layer empirical study of an open-set outdoor 3DSG (Terra) across five real outdoor datasets, with new multi-run consistency metrics and a context-aware object query for small VLMs.
insight: Per-point CLIP embeddings are often multimodal, not just noisy: about 30% of points have outlier ratio >0.1, HDBSCAN silhouette is around 0.5, and some points have up to 100 clusters, so plain averaging discards semantics. Averaging also hurts regions: only 2 of 68 ground-truth region nodes scored higher than all their children. Navigation failures came only from untraversable terrain (place graph has no traversability), and the strict/relaxed gap came from the closest-place-node goal choice, not from the VLM. Prompt wording matters a lot (negation prompt F1 0.152 vs clarification 0.707).
method: Terra 3DSG (case study, not new): LIO-SAM voxel map with CLIP embeddings from FastSAM masks and YOLO terrain labels; terrain-GVD place nodes; region nodes by agglomerative or spectral clustering; A* on place graph
Embedding analysis: per-point modified z-score outliers on cosine distance to mean (threshold 3.5) and HDBSCAN clustering with silhouette score to find multiple semantic modes
Object+Context query: retrieve all bounding boxes for the object name (MS-Max), attach the nearest place node, re-rank by 0.7 object similarity + 0.3 place-node context similarity
Navigation protocol: GPS localization in the 3DSG, A* over place nodes to top-1 (fallback top-2/3), wheelchair manually driven along waypoints; strict/relaxed success and path efficiency
Region querying protocol: human-labelled regions, top-k region nodes for k=1..15, micro/macro P/R/F1, plus prompt-variation study

Consistency metrics: NCR (node count ratio), NCC (clustering consistency), NCS (place-node cosine similarity), TMC (terrain match), Dist (place-node distance), computed across 4 repeated RV Park runs after ICP/GICP alignment
Memory analysis: pickle size of the Terra object vs mapped area (occupancy-grid area)

setting.backbone: CLIP (frozen) + FastSAM + YOLO terrain segmenter (trained on GOOSE/GOOSE-Ex); Terra pipeline with A* planner
setting.training_data: YOLO terrain model trained on GOOSE and GOOSE-Ex; CLIP/FastSAM used as pretrained; no new training for the study
setting.observation: 3 monocular OAK-D LR cameras (90° apart, 10 Hz) + Ouster OS1-128 LiDAR + IMU
setting.action_space: waypoints from A* over place-node graph (GPS waypoints), manually driven wheelchair
setting.privileged: GPS-to-3DSG transform (from satellite imagery alignment) for localization; manual driving; manually annotated GT object locations and regions for evaluation

numbers.eval_set_note: 14 of 17 object prompts (those correctly detected), 3 start nodes each = 42 trials over 4 datasets (Rock Canyon omitted)
numbers.extra: GPS localization, manual driving along planned waypoints, success radius 10 m, top-1 place node
numbers.evidence: Table 'Real-World 3DSG-Based Object Navigation Results', Summary row: 42 trials, 0.548, 0.691, 0.66 (±0.17)

numbers.extra: relaxed success, manually verified, 17 contextualized prompts

numbers.eval_set_note: River Park, 4 regions, avg over k=1..15
numbers.evidence: Table 'Region Querying Results', River Park Agglomerative row

numbers_note: Not a standard benchmark paper; results are on the authors' own outdoor datasets. Per-dataset region results (Nunns, Marina P1/P2, Rock Canyon) and consistency metrics are in tables/figures; the abstract's macro F1 ~0.359 is a summary; consistency results are only in figures.
results: Outdoor Terra 3DSG navigation achieved SS-1 0.548 / RS-1 0.691 over 42 real trials with about 66% path efficiency; Object+Context beat Object Only (RS-1 0.647) and Full Sentence (0.529) with RS-1 0.765. Region querying F1 is low (around 0.36 average, worst on Rock Canyon at 0.14-0.24), memory stays under 600 MB for a 3 km trajectory, and multi-run consistency is reasonable (NCR/NCS near 1, TMC/NCC above 0.5, worst Dist 2.58 m).
limitations: Case study of a single 3DSG system (Terra) with a small CLIP-based VLM; generalization to other 3DSGs is untested
Navigation is manually driven with GPS localization, small trial count (42), and no traversability in the place graph
Region ground truth comes from a single annotator and is subjective; data was collected in fall/winter with leaves as a terrain class
